articles.deck: Organizers expect about 9 people and say summer concert series is the main draw.
body: Hannah Lacey, who has lived on Ingram Street for 9 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected. The Stonebridge Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.
Organizers say the work is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Monday mornings. Anyone interested can attend the next planning meeting at the Millrace library on Monday at 7 p.m.

articles.title: Then & Now: Lilac Street in 1985 and Today
articles.deck: A photo from the Millrace County Historical Society shows the same corner as it looked decades ago.
body: A 1985 photograph from the Millrace County Historical Society shows Lilac Street from the corner of Oak Avenue. Someone took the same picture from the same spot this month, holding the camera at about the same height.
Most of the houses are still standing, though the porches and the trees have changed a good deal.

body: Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days. Councilmember Agnes Szabo asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $25,000.

articles.title: Letter: The Neighborhood Watch Sign Program on Wren Place Needs Attention
body: To the editor: I have lived on Wren Place for 20 years, and I want to say what a difference the Foxglove Heights Neighbors has made.
I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the May meeting. Please keep the neighborhood watch sign program in the budget. Many of us on Wren Place use it every week.
Stella Ingersoll, Foundry Row

articles.deck: The program begins in September and is open to all students in grade 6 and up.
